AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND AND AIMS
AbstractText.content: Most cases of colorectal cancer develop via an adenoma to carcinoma sequence. Gallbladder polyps share some risk factors with colorectal polyps. Little is known about the relationship between gallbladder diseases and different status of colorectal polyps by gender. This study was to investigate the association of gallbladder stones and polyps with colorectal adenomas by gender in a Taiwanese population.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: We recruited 7,066 eligible subjects who underwent a total colonoscopy as a part of health check-up between Jan 2001 and August 2009. Colonoscopic findings were classified into polyp-free, non-neoplastic polyps and colorectal adenomas. Gallbladder stones and gallbladder polyps were diagnosed based on ultrasonographic findings.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: There was a significant difference in the status of colon polyps between subjects with and without gallbladder polyps. However, the status of colon polyps was not significantly different between subjects with or without gallbladder stones. After adjusting obesity, fasting plasma glucose and other variables, there was a positive relationship between gallbladder polyps and colorectal adenomas (OR: 1.396, 95% CI: 1.115-1.747) but not non-neoplastic polyps in all subjects. In males, gallbladder polyps (OR: 1.560, 95% CI: 1.204-2.019) and gallbladder stones (OR: 1.465, 95% CI 1.081-1.984) were positively associated with colorectal adenomas. In females, neither gallbladder polyps nor gallbladder stones were significantly related to colon polyps.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: Both gallbladder polyps and gallbladder stones were associated with an increased risk of colorectal adenomas in males but not in females. Gender difference was significant for the association between gallbladder lesions and colorectal polyps.
